text: Debugging is a crucial skill for any programmer. When a program doesn’t work as expected, the first step is identifying the bug. This means reading error messages carefully and narrowing down which part of the code causes the problem. Instead of guessing, a systematic approach works best: reproduce the issue, form a hypothesis, and test it step by step. Debugging tools, like breakpoints and debuggers, let you pause the program and inspect variable values. Additionally, logging—adding print statements or writing to a log file—helps track the flow of execution. With patience and a clear method, you can solve even the trickiest bugs.
